classification.difficultyReason: Select SAS, RHS or AAS from marked diagrams and recognise insufficient non-included-angle data.

content.prompt: In each part below, if the two triangles are congruent, write down the congruence statement, giving the appropriate congruence test as a reason.

spec.description: Paired oblique triangles with double ticks JK and XY, triple ticks JL and XZ, and equal included angles at J and X. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: J corresponds to X, K to Y, L to Z; SAS.

answer.worked: $JK=XY$ and $JL=XZ$ (marked sides), and $\angle KJL=\angle YXZ=\alpha$ (included angles). Hence $\triangle KJL\equiv\triangle YXZ$ (SAS).

spec.description: Two right triangles with squares at S and W, double ticks ST and UW and triple ticks RT and UV. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: Equal hypotenuses RT and UV, equal sides ST and WU; RHS.

answer.worked: $\angle RST=\angle VWU=90^\circ$, $RT=VU$ (hypotenuses) and $ST=WU$ (marked sides). Hence $\triangle RST\equiv\triangle VWU$ (RHS).

spec.description: Paired triangles EDF and MLK with double and triple side ticks; theta at F and M is non-included. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: Two corresponding sides and a non-included angle do not guarantee congruence.

answer.worked: The marked equal angles are not included between the two marked sides. Two sides and a non-included angle do not establish congruence.

spec.description: Paired right triangles retaining 7 cm and 8 cm perpendicular sides and all vertex labels. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: AJ=KO=8 cm, JZ=OR=7 cm, included right angles J and O.

answer.worked: $AJ=KO=8$ cm, $JZ=OR=7$ cm and $\angle AJZ=\angle KOR=90^\circ$. Hence $\triangle AJZ\equiv\triangle KOR$ (SAS).

spec.description: Differently oriented paired triangles with 10 m and 7 m sides and leaders to the narrow included 20 degree angles. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: HS=BY=7 m, SI=YT=10 m, included angles at S and Y are 20 degrees.

answer.worked: $HS=BY=7$ m, $SI=YT=10$ m and $\angle HSI=\angle BYT=20^\circ$. Hence $\triangle HSI\equiv\triangle BYT$ (SAS).

spec.description: Paired right triangles with hypotenuses 3 km, right angles A and K, 70 degrees at B and 20 degrees at W. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: Angle C=20 degrees and angle L=70 degrees; AAS with corresponding hypotenuses.

answer.worked: $\angle C=180^\circ-90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ$ (angle sum of a triangle). Thus $\angle A=\angle K=90^\circ$, $\angle C=\angle W=20^\circ$ and $BC=LW=3$ km. Hence $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle KLW$ (AAS).
